item.title: Former Real Madrid star amazed by Bellingham after win vs Celta Vigo: ‘Best midfielder in the world’
item.description: Former Real Madrid star amazed by Bellingham after win vs Celta Vigo: ‘Best midfielder in the world’ After a season in which he appeared below his best level, Real Madrid superstar Jude Bellingham appears to have returned to his peak this campaign. One of the main objectives for manager Jose Mourinho when he took over the reins in the summer was to help the England international regain his mojo after a year disrupted by injuries, confusion over his role, and inconsistent displays. And, judging by how things have been going, it is safe to say that the 23-year-old is once again looking like one of the most influential players in the world. The latest display of his quality came on Saturday when he helped Real Madrid secure a 2-1 comeback win over Celta Vigo at the Santiago Bernabeu, scoring the equalising goal in the second half. Alvaro Benito left stunned by Bellingham Following the match, former Real Madrid player Alvaro Benito was effusive in praise of Bellingham, stating that the England star was enjoying his best moment at the club and was the best in the world in his position. Bellingham starred for Real Madrid against Celta Vigo. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images) “We are witnessing the best version of Bellingham. He has an influence on the game that he didn’t have before; now he’s a complete player,” Benito said on Cadena SER (h/t AS ). He also highlighted the mentality that separates Bellingham from other players, saying: “For me, he’s the best midfielder in the world; he’s capable of doing everything. Of all his virtues, the greatest is his ambition and his winning, competitive mentality. For me, without a doubt, this is Bellingham’s best moment at Real Madrid.” Vinicius and other teammates join in praise Bellingham, for his goal and overall contributions last night, was named the Man of the Match against Celta Vigo. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Jude Bellingham (@judebellingham) Following the match, the Real Madrid superstar shared a post on Instagram, prompting several of his teammates to respond with messages of admiration. Vinicius Jr. wrote: “You’re the best,” while youngster Thiago Pitarch added: “Another level.” Real Madrid’s other hero against Celta Vigo, Carlos Espi, responded: “What a show.” Injured forward Rodrygo also joined in, writing: “What a player.” The result also saw Bellingham achieve a special milestone as he recorded his 100th La Liga victory with Real Madrid. Given his impact and influence, it does not come as a surprise to see Real Madrid working to extend Bellingham’s contract until 2032 .

item.title: Colorado’s 380-pound guard Chauncey Gooden took down more than a Cincinnati player defending a teammate
item.description: The Colorado Buffaloes saw their bowl hopes end Saturday with a 35-28 loss to the Cincinnati Bearcats at Nippert Stadium, and one of the afternoon’s most-shared clips belonged to a 380-pound offensive lineman. Late in the game, Cincinnati’s Antwan Peek Jr. stood over a Colorado receiver who was down after a play. As an official moved in to pull Peek away, Chauncey Gooden charged in and took down both Peek and the official. Players from both teams rushed in before officials separated them, and Deion Sanders stepped into the scrum to send his players away. Chauncey Gooden got his teammates back https://t.co/O9WFxWnIwC — Grant Reacts (@GrantReacts1) November 21, 2026 Coach Prime Had To Get In Between Colorado Players And Cincinnati Players After The Game. Oh Boy… https://t.co/YNqyTHxPBD — SM Highlights (@SMHighlights1) November 21, 2026 Colorado had come to Ohio off a 42-32 upset of the then-No. 14 Houston Cougars, then turned the ball over four times on Saturday. Isaac Wilson threw three interceptions, and Cole Tabb scored four touchdowns as Cincinnati became bowl eligible and won in November for the first time since 2024 after 12 straight losses in the month. Travel problems the day before the game had put the Buffaloes behind before they arrived. Apr 11, 2026; Boulder, CO, USA; Colorado Buffaloes head coach Deion Sanders before the start of the spring game at Folsom Field. Mandatory Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images “Early in the game, we didn’t show up. We were still on the tarmac. Early turnovers crippled us,” Sanders said. He put the rest of the result on himself. “We just have no true consistency. We don’t know at this point how we’re going to show up. Is the offense going to show up, the defense going to show up, the special teams. All of it’s on me,” Sanders said . Who is Chauncey Gooden? Gooden is a second-year guard from Nashville who played at Lipscomb Academy and has started every game he has appeared in this season. After an Aug. 10 practice, assistant offensive line coach George Hegamin said there was “a lot more aggression and a lot more violence up front” and named Gooden as the lineman who brings that intent. A week before the trip to Cincinnati, Gooden was part of the line, with Xavier Payne, Sean Kinney, Leon Bell and Larry Johnson III, named the Big 12 Offensive Line of the Week after the Buffaloes ran 39 times for 249 yards and five touchdowns without allowing a sack in the win over Houston. Colorado managed 67 rushing yards in the first half and 121 for the game, and the loss dropped the Buffaloes to 4-7, guaranteeing a third losing season in Sanders’ four years in Boulder and a second straight year without a bowl. It was also Colorado’s 10th straight loss in Big 12 road games. In a season with little left to play for, Gooden’s most visible moment in Cincinnati came after a play was over, standing up for a teammate on the turf. item.description: The Tennessee Volunteers beat the LSU Tigers 27-13 at Neyland Stadium on Saturday night, and with 3:14 left, the game stopped because of what came out of the stands. After a pass interference call gave LSU a first down at the Tennessee 30, fans threw golf balls, mustard bottles and other debris onto the field, and LSU’s players left their sideline until it was cleared. The objects were the same ones that rained down in October 2021, the last time Lane Kiffin brought a visiting team to Knoxville. His Ole Miss Rebels won 31-26 that night, Kiffin was hit by a golf ball, and University of Tennessee police reported 18 arrests and 47 ejections. The SEC fined Tennessee $250,000 , and the school banned 16 students and nine other fans from its athletic events. item.title: Kirk Ferentz makes feelings on CFP committee clear after Iowa’s 34-17 win at Illinois
item.description: The Iowa Hawkeyes beat the Illinois Fighting Illini 34-17 in Champaign on Saturday to move to 9-2 without leading rusher Kamari Moulton, who is out for the season, taking control early and answering every time Illinois scored. Kirk Ferentz had barely left the field when Big Ten Network sideline reporter Brooke Fletcher asked what a win like that could show the College Football Playoff selection committee. Iowa came into the weekend at No. 15 in the committee’s rankings, the same spot it held a week earlier. A 28-7 win over the Purdue Boilermakers, Iowa’s third straight Big Ten win by a combined 82-17 , had left the Hawkeyes in place while the Oregon Ducks and Ohio State Buckeyes moved past them. Nov 11, 2023; Iowa City, Iowa, USA; Iowa Hawkeyes head coach Kirk Ferentz reacts during the fourth quarter against the Rutgers Scarlet Knights at Kinnick Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jeffrey Becker-USA TODAY Sports “I swear to God, I could care less about those guys. They’re gonna do what they want to do, and I really don’t care. Our goal is to come in here and win. It’s not easy winning in college football. It’s not easy on the road, conference game, so go right down the list, so I’m just really happy for our guys,” Ferentz told Fletcher. “I swear to God, I could care less about those guys. They’re gonna do what they want to do, and I really don’t care.” Iowa’s Kirk Ferentz on the CFP committee https://t.co/4LHs8zTIK4 — Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) November 21, 2026 Iowa beat Purdue by three touchdowns and held it to a single score, and the win did nothing for its ranking. The questions about style points followed the team to Illinois anyway. A committee that left a 28-7 Big Ten win unrewarded gives Ferentz little reason to chase margins now. Iowa’s two losses include a rivalry defeat that still shapes how its season is judged. The Minnesota Golden Gophers beat the Hawkeyes 13-10 on a field goal as time expired on Oct. 24, a game in which Iowa turned the ball over four times and changed quarterbacks, with Hank Brown replacing Jeremy Hecklinski in the second quarter. Iowa has won every game since. What can still move Iowa into the playoff field? No. 4 UCLA fell 18-16 in triple overtime at Michigan, the Indiana Hoosiers lost, and Ohio State, one of the two teams that jumped Iowa last week, fell 31-28 at Nebraska for its fourth loss of the season. Those results did more for Iowa than its own score. That Nebraska Cornhuskers team comes to Kinnick Stadium for Iowa’s regular-season finale on Friday, Nov. 27, at noon ET. A week ago, beating Nebraska would have looked like a routine rivalry win to close the season. It now means beating the team that just ended Ohio State’s playoff hopes, which gives Iowa’s resume something the committee can point to without Ferentz ever making the argument himself. item.title: What Bob Chesney told UCLA players in the locker room after triple-overtime loss to Michigan
item.description: Bob Chesney had gone 10 games at UCLA without addressing a losing locker room. That ended Saturday night at Michigan Stadium, where the Michigan Wolverines beat the No. 4 UCLA Bruins 18-16 in three overtimes and cost them a chance to clinch a spot in the Big Ten championship game. UCLA scored one touchdown all night, with 10 seconds left in regulation. Ty Dieffenbach threw an interception in the red zone in the first quarter and was strip-sacked while the Bruins were driving late in the first half. One of his two lost fumbles set up Michigan’s go-ahead touchdown early in the fourth quarter. In overtime, UCLA settled for two field goals before Madden Iamaleava’s two-point pass fell incomplete in the third period. Oct 17, 2026; Pasadena, California, USA; UCLA Bruins head coach Bob Chesney in the first half against the Wisconsin Badgers at the Rose Bowl. Mandatory Credit: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images “This was a battle, and obviously we came up a little bit short, and like we always say, we have to find a way to get better, period. That’s it, no excuses. I thought they played a really good game of football. We know they were tough. “The message in the locker room was nobody hang your head. You played a really good team, and you battled with that team, and then we came up a little short. “When you have your opportunity, you’ve got to make the most of it against a really good defense like that. And we just didn’t do it,” Chesney said . Bob Chesney on UCLA’s loss at Michigan: “The message in the locker room was nobody hang your head. You played a really good team & you battled… When you have your opportunity, you’ve got to make the most of it against a really good defense like that. And we just didn’t do it.” https://t.co/3UDwFXMq1O — The Next Round (@NextRoundLive) November 22, 2026 The 16 points were UCLA’s lowest total of the season. Chesney said afterward that the Bruins cannot give the ball away the way they did near the goal line, where the turnovers took points off the board. A defense that held Michigan to one touchdown in regulation gave UCLA enough to win. Who will play quarterback for UCLA against USC? The answer depends on Dieffenbach, who was carted off after a 6-yard run on the first play of overtime. Chesney had no update on the injury after the game. Dieffenbach had taken over as the starter after Nico Iamaleava’s season-ending knee injury in October, which leaves Madden Iamaleava, Nico’s younger brother, as the next option. “It’s tough to lose anybody. It’s the brand, the game that we play. We all understand that it’s really hard to make it through the whole season unscathed. Not the greatest moment to lose him. But at the same point, we have to trust Madden. He’s got to be able to deliver in those moments,” Chesney said . item.title: 2. Bundesliga: Hertha cruise to 4-0 derby victory over Cottbus
item.description: 2. Bundesliga: Hertha cruise to 4-0 derby victory over Cottbus Stefan Leitl’s side arrived at the LEAG Energie Stadion looking to build on their impressive 2-1 victory over promotion rivals Wolfsburg before the international break, and they made the perfect start to the Berlin-Brandenburg derby. The visitors needed just six minutes to break the deadlock, with Sebastian Grønning rising highest to head home Mads Pedersen’s corner from close range. Cottbus attempted to respond, with Justin Butler testing Marius Gersbeck from distance, while the hosts were briefly awarded a penalty in the 23rd minute after Deyovaisio Zeefuik appeared to handle inside the area. However, referee Florian Exner overturned his initial decision following a VAR review, ruling that the Hertha defender’s arm had been in a natural position. Energie thought they had found an equaliser shortly afterwards when Lucas Copado found the net following a set-piece, but the effort was ruled out for offside. Despite Cottbus showing some resistance, Hertha remained in control and almost doubled their advantage before the interval when Grønning was denied from close range by Marcel Lotka. The visitors did not have to wait long after the restart to extend their lead. Just three minutes into the second half, Jón Dagur Thorsteinsson flicked on a corner at the near post, allowing Paul Seguin to arrive unmarked and head home from close range. Cottbus’ hopes of mounting a comeback were dealt another significant blow in the 58th minute when Fousseny Doumbia was shown a straight red card for bringing down Thorsteinsson as the last defender. With a numerical advantage, Hertha were able to manage the remainder of the contest with relative comfort, Kevin Sessa came close to adding a third when his follow-up effort flew over the crossbar. The visitors eventually put the result beyond doubt in the closing stages, with Deyovaisio Zeefuik making it 3-0 in the 90th minute before substitute Gustaf Nilsson completed the scoring moments later. The Swedish forward’s strike was particularly memorable, marking his first goal for Hertha since joining the club. The emphatic victory means Hertha remain unbeaten after 12 league matches, having collected 34 points from a possible 36. They now hold a ten-point advantage over second-placed Nürnberg and are firmly establishing themselves as the early favourites for promotion. Cottbus, meanwhile, remain without a victory in their last seven league matches and sit 17th in the table with 11 points, continuing their difficult run since the start of the campaign.

item.title: “What the Unemployed Sound Like”: Landry Kiffin Gives Brutal Reply to Tennessee Crowd for Going After Dad Lane Kiffin
item.description: Sep 27, 2025; Oxford, Mississippi, USA; Mississippi Rebels head coach Lane Kiffin poses for a photo with his daughter Landry Kiffin prior to the game against the LSU Tigers at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium. © Petre Thomas-Imagn Images It wasn’t a happy return to his old stomping grounds for Lane Kiffin as LSU was humbled 27-13 by Tennessee in Knoxville, and the fans’ hatred for their former head coach was visible as they created a raucous atmosphere inside Neyland stadium. Vols fans took over the game at multiple times, making their feelings about Kiffin known as they tossed objects onto the field, including golf balls, mustard bottles and other trash, and after the game, Lane Kiffin’s daughter Landry Kiffin’s support for her dad became public. Landry posted on social media platform TikTok about her experience with the fans, referring to them as “unemployed” as she walked around the stadium. “Rent free,” Landry captioned the video, as also posted by Jack Mac . “In case you’re wondering what the unemployed sound like,” she also wrote. Lane Kiffin Spoke About the Impact of the Crowd After the Game Lane Kiffin acknowledged that the crowd played a major role in his team being unable to get going against Tennessee. When asked about what LSU does in training to battle something like this, Kiffin explained his usual exercise. “I mean, we put the speakers right behind us and everything. And so again, we’ve been doing this for years and I just think that they somehow hit a level that’s louder. Plus, some players have louder claps. Quarterbacks over time,” Kiffin remarked in the postgame press conference. He further said he doesn’t feel it’ll be an issue going forward, but doesn’t want to motivate Arkansas, LSU’s next opponents. “I don’t think it’ll be an issue. I don’t want to motivate Arkansas, but I don’t think it’ll be an issue. They’re the same. Otherwise if you could redo it, you know, you’d look at different, you know, cadence from the offensive line.” The loss means LSU’s record stands at 6-5 now, and they need to pick up a win against Arkansas in the team’s next clash on Saturday. item.title: Sun Belt Week 12 Takeaways: Nearing the End
item.description: Photo credit: Marshall Athletics | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Kate Pearson Halyburton, Editor With the 2026 college football regular season coming to an end, the Sun Belt Conference saw several teams effectively play for their seasons. Some games ended in blowouts, while one went down to the final seconds. Bowl eligibility and division leads were on the line. Let’s see how this week went for teams with a lot to play for. Sun Belt Week 12 Recap Georgia State at Marshall This matchup between Georgia State and Marshall was huge for both teams’ bowl eligibility aspirations. Let’s say both teams came to play, and this one went all the way down to the wire. The Thundering Herd ended up escaping with the victory over the Panthers, 28-27. Down seven with 10 seconds left, Ayden Pereira found Rodshaun Dorsey on a Hail Mary in the back of the end zone for the touchdown. Unfortunately for the Panthers, they missed the extra point to tie the game, leading to a tough loss. Quarterback Carlos Del Rio-Wilson started his first game for the Thundering Herd since Oct. 10. While he only completed 12 of 23 passes, he did throw three touchdowns and ran for an additional touchdown. The Thundering Herd gained bowl eligibility with this victory and head into next week’s game against Louisiana-Monroe with considerably less pressure. For the Panthers, there were some very good things that they showcased in this one, specifically on offense. Pereira had a much better showing than last week, and the run game was productive. The one mistake the Panthers would love to take back is the interception at the end of the first half by Pereira. While it didn’t lead to any points for the Thundering Herd, they were in field goal range and could have added three points; judging by the final score, those points would have been vital. item.description: Jul 29, 2025; Bronx, New York, USA; New York Yankees relief pitcher Jonathan Loaisiga (43) reacts as he walks off the field after the top of the eighth inning against the Tampa Bay Rays at Yankee Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Brad Penner-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Jonathan Loaisiga went to Arizona and did the thing the Yankees spent years waiting to see: he took the ball for a full season. Mark Feinsand reported Friday for MLB.com that the right-hander agreed to return on a two-year deal worth about $18 million, with a club option for 2029. The report said the deal was pending a physical; the Yankees had not announced it. I’d make that deal, with one caveat. Let Loaisiga start clean innings. Don’t make the entire middle of the bullpen depend on his ability to work on short rest and escape somebody else’s trouble. Sep 23, 2026; Denver, Colorado, USA; Arizona Diamondbacks pitcher Jonathan Loaisiga (43) delivers a pitch in the ninth inning against the Colorado Rockies at Coors Field. Mandatory Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect What the Yankees would be paying for Loaisiga had a 2.42 ERA over 67 innings in 67 appearances for Arizona, according to his MLB record . He didn’t get there by blowing everybody away. Feinsand’s report put his strikeout rate at 18.4% and his walk rate at 5%. Baseball Savant’s contact profile shows why that combination worked: 55.8% ground balls and a 3.5% barrel rate. Those numbers matter in a clean seventh. Loaisiga can attack the first hitter instead of having to make a perfect pitch with a runner already in scoring position. If a hitter rolls over his sinker, he can get an out without getting deep into the count. He can also use a changeup off the sinker when a hitter is ready to swing at the harder pitch. It is a practical way to get three outs without trying to win every at-bat with a strikeout. The success wasn’t confined to one good month. Across his last 30 regular-season appearances he walked six in 32 2/3 innings. He also threw two scoreless innings against the Yankees on September 20. Those are two different snapshots from the same season, and neither tells you what his arm will do in April. The Yankees should still have an option for an inherited-runner spot where a strikeout is particularly valuable. item.title: Blackburn rally without Tony Mowbray to deny Burnley long-awaited home win
item.description: Todd Cantwell’s penalty earned Blackburn a 2-2 draw at Burnley in their first match since head coach Tony Mowbray stepped back because of health issues . In a gripping, physical East Lancashire derby, the home side led twice, through Largie Ramazani’s rising first-half drive and Jaydon Banel’s steered finish after the break. But Andri Gudjohnsen scored Blackburn’s first equaliser, then earned the penalty which Cantwell converted. Burnley remain deep in relegation trouble, without a home league victory for 400 days, having once again failed to hold on to a lead. They have now dropped 25 points from winning positions in the Championship this season. Blackburn wanted a victory not just for local pride, but to honour Mowbray, who turned 63 on Sunday, and for whom this was set to be a 900th match in management before his announcement on Tuesday that he would be stepping back. Their players warmed up in T-shirts bearing the message ‘We’re with you, Tony’ on the back and the number 900 on the front. Blackburn honoured Tony Mowbray before kick-off (PA) Coaches Damien Johnson and Mike Dodds have taken charge in Mowbray’s absence and had to reshuffle the defence when Tom Atcheson was concussed after receiving a boot to the face in the third minute. Stand-in goalkeeper Aynsley Pears, playing after Balazs Toth suffered a broken hand on international duty with Hungary, pushed over a fierce deflected shot from Banel, but was at fault when Ramazani gave Burnley a 27th-minute lead. The on-loan Leeds winger cut in from the right and fired a shot that flew into the roof of the net right by Pears, who was too slow to react. But Gudjohnsen equalised four minutes later, racing on to a Harry Pickering long ball that drifted over Burnley centre-back Max Alleyne, and steering a sweet shot beyond goalkeeper Max Weiss for his 12th goal of the season. The Icelander celebrated by grabbing a T-shirt paying tribute to Mowbray from a photographer and displaying it for the cameras. Andri Gudjohnsen paid tribute to Mowbray while celebrating his equaliser (PA) Blackburn finished the first half strongly, with Cantwell firing over a good chance, before Banel restored Burnley’s lead six minutes into the second half, running unchallenged to place a shot into the far corner as defender Hayden Carter backed off. The home side were fortunate to escape a strong penalty appeal just before the hour mark as Cantwell burst into the penalty area and saw two attempted crosses both strike the arm of Igor Julio. Blackburn did get a penalty with 16 minutes left as Josh Laurent, attempting to clear a low cross, failed to spot Gudjohnsen darting in from behind him and caught the striker’s leg. Cantwell drove the penalty straight down the middle to make it 2-2. Gudjohnsen thought he had given Blackburn the lead two minutes later, when he controlled and drove a low shot against the base of the post with Weiss a spectator, but neither side could find a winner.

That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter. Scott Taetsch via Getty Images United remains one of three MLS organizations without a developmental team bridging the youth academy to the first team. Efforts to build a complex in Baltimore for an MLS Next Pro operation have floundered. (Meanwhile, United's owners have launched a pro volleyball team.)
